title.title: The ionization conjecture
title.subtitle: Claim: $M$ nuclei of total charge $Z$ bind at most $Z + CM$ electrons, with one universal constant $C$

beats.text: How many electrons beyond $Z$ can one nucleus bind? Upper bounds so far
Lieb $2Z + 1$, Nam $1.22Z + 3Z^{1/3}$, Fefferman–Seco $Z + O(Z^{5/7})$; constants schematic
Claim: the excess is a universal constant per nucleus, $N \le Z + CM$

achievement.label: The ionization conjecture (on Simon's list, 2000)
achievement.note: $C$ is not explicit; strict binding only

verify.detail: Lean: the $m^{7/3}$ ionization-energy and outer-radius asymptotics. Not $N \le Z + CM$
verify.ourCheck: We compared the Lean scope with the claim; we did not build it

sources.quote: Lieb N<2Z+M (Phys. Rev. A 1984); Nam N<1.22Z+3Z^{1/3} (Commun. Math. Phys. 312, 2012)
listed by Simon in 'Schrodinger operators in the twenty-first century' (2000)
The best theorems said roughly $2Z$ (Lieb 1984) and then $1.22Z + 3Z^{1/3}$

plain: How many extra electrons can an atom hold? Experiments say one or two; this claims at most a fixed number

steps: Look at the outer electrons from beyond a fixed radius
There they see an almost neutral system: charges screen out
A neutral system holds few extras: a constant per nucleus

voice.text: Proven bounds allowed about twice the charge. Experiments suggest just one or two extra.
Far out, the outer electrons see an almost neutral atom, capping the excess.
Claimed: at most a constant extra per nucleus.
